messages.author: 778abaa663647a33
messages.subject: Re: MRDS and MCDS detection probability
parts:
Marina-

I'm not entirely following what you are doing with density but the fitted
detection curves are the same. The differences you are seeing in the
coefficients are for two reasons. The intercept is treated differently in
the 2 models and the factors are using different reference levels which is
why the signs are flipped on the beaufort and beau coefficients. The
intercept in the MCDS is not on the log scale. It is
exp(6.00467-1.261+1.11528)=350.3.

Had the coefficients been truly different then you would not have gotten
the same value of Pa. With regard to the cv, I'm unsure why those are
different and I'd have to look at the data further. Maybe others or you can
explain further where the differences in density are occurring. Is it
between mrds and mcds or between one of those and calculations you made?

--jeff
